m: Warm and friendly.
t: Same as « cordial »: from the heart (cœur).

m: To instruct or improve morally or intellectually.
t: Same as « édifier »: build up the mind, like building an édifice.

m: Lacking physical strength; weak.
t: Feeble = « faible » (feble → faible).

m: Well chosen or apt; pleasing.
t: Une formule heureuse: a felicitous phrase fits perfectly. Cousin of « félicité ».

m: To refrain from; to hold back.
t: Bear back your anger. Not to be confused with « forebear » (ancestor).

m: Motivated primarily by money.
t: Same as « mercenaire »: acting only for the pay.

m: Characterized by peculiar or unconventional traits.
t: A quirk is a petite manie: a quirky sense of humour.

m: Characterized by conflict, disorder or confusion.
t: Same as « turbulent ».

m: A direct opposite; a contrast of ideas.
t: Same as « antithèse »: placed against.

m: Unable to think clearly; confused.
e: From be- + fuddle (to confuse, probably drink-related), origin unclear.
t: Fuddled brain, as if drunk: « l'esprit brouillé ».

m: To make an action or process happen sooner or be accomplished more quickly.
t: Free the feet and go: « expédier » une affaire. Opposite of impede.

m: To pretend to be affected by (a feeling or state).
t: Same as « feindre ».

m: Absolutely necessary.
t: Same as « indispensable ».

m: Existing only in part; biased, or fond of something.
t: Three senses: incomplete (partiel), biased (partial), and « partial to » = fond of.

m: Engaged in deep or serious thought.
t: Same as « pensif ».

m: To be an omen or warning of.
t: Same family as « portent » (a bad sign): dark clouds portend a storm.

m: Beneficial, especially when unpleasant.
t: Same as « salutaire »: a salutary lesson.

m: To cut off; to end a connection.
t: Related to « sevrer » and « séparer »: sever ties.

m: Sleepy; inducing drowsiness.
t: Same as « somnolent »: somnus = sleep.

m: Enduring pain or hardship without showing feelings.
t: Same as « stoïque ».

m: To decrease gradually in size, strength or power.
t: The moon wanes (« décroît »). Opposite: wax.

m: Noisy, energetic and cheerful.
t: Not « boisson ». A boisterous party is rowdy.

m: Kept secret, especially because illicit.
t: Same as « clandestin ».

m: Making someone weak and infirm.
t: From « débile » (weak), not stupid: a debilitating illness drains strength.

m: Deferential respect; a gesture of submission.
t: Obéissance + « révérence »: a deep bow.

m: Full of danger or risk.
t: Same as « périlleux ».

m: Aggressively greedy or grasping.
t: Same as « rapace »: a bird of prey. Rapacious landlords seize everything.

m: To enjoy greatly.
e: Old French relais (something left behind, a savour), from relaisser.
t: Relish a meal = savourer. (Also n.: a condiment.)

m: Using irony or mockery to expose folly.
t: Same as « satirique »: Charlie Hebdo.

m: Something fake presented as genuine.
t: A sham marriage: a « mariage blanc ». A fake.

m: To avoid dealing with; to go around the edge of.
t: The skirt is the edge of the garment: you go around the edge. Skirt the issue = contourner.

m: Slow-moving; lacking energy.
t: Like a slug (limace): a sluggish economy.

m: Angry and bitter.
t: Same as « acrimonieux »: sharp (acre) words.

m: Doing good; generous.
t: Bene + facere = « bienfaisant ».

m: Shrewd, especially in money matters.
t: Knows how to: a canny investor. Cousin of « cunning ».

m: Suffering anxiety or pain; (of goods) sold at a low price; (of furniture) aged on purpose.
t: Détresse. But distressed jeans are artificially worn.

m: Diminishing gradually.
t: Dwindling supplies are slowly vanishing: « s'amenuiser ».

m: To obscure or surpass in importance.
t: Same as « éclipser »: a star outshines the others.

m: Comprehensive in scope.
t: Same as « encyclopédique »: knowing everything.

m: Intensely irritated.
t: Same as « exaspéré ».

m: Replaceable by another identical item; interchangeable.
e: Medieval Latin fungibilis, from fungi vice (to perform in place of).
t: Fongible: a euro is fungible, a painting is not.

m: Able to be exchanged with each other.
t: Same as « interchangeable ».

m: Producing a great deal of profit.
t: Same as « lucratif ».

m: Of secondary importance; on the edge.
t: Périphérique (le boulevard!) = the ring around the middle.

m: Causing a strong reaction, especially anger or arousal.
t: Same as « provocant ».

m: To formally give up or reject.
t: Same as « renoncer ».

m: Able to be defended against attack or objection.
t: Tenable = « tenable »: a position you can hold. Untenable = indéfendable.

m: A natural liking or attraction; similarity.
t: Same as « affinité »: « avoir des affinités ».

m: Showing selfless concern for others.
t: Same as « altruiste ».

m: Highly ornate and extravagant.
t: Same as « baroque »: complex and over-decorated.

m: To weaken or damage; to settle by mutual concession.
t: Two uses: reach a compromise, OR « compromettre » (compromise safety = endanger it).

m: To tolerate or approve; (n.) the face.
t: Contenance. As a verb: « ne pas cautionner ». I will not countenance such behaviour.

m: Able to be believed; convincing.
t: Same as « crédible ».

m: Spread over a wide area; not concise. (v. diffuse = to spread)
t: Same as « diffus »: a diffuse writing style never gets to the point.

m: Consisting of documents; based on factual evidence.
t: Documentary evidence = « preuves documentaires ».

m: Examining or including all elements; thorough.
t: Same as « exhaustif »: leave nothing out. Not « exhausting ».

m: Making one feel very happy, animated or elated.
t: Hilarious inside: hilaris. An exhilarating rollercoaster.

m: Intense and passionate feeling.
t: Same as « ferveur ».

m: Based on illusion; not real.
t: Same as « illusoire ».

m: Used in a figurative sense, not literal.
t: Same as « métaphorique ».

m: To imitate, especially to ridicule.
t: Mimic = « mime »: act like someone else.

m: Having a strong religious or spiritual quality; awe-inspiring.
t: Numen = divinity. Sensing a god in a cathedral.

m: Based on reason or logic.
t: Same as « rationnel ».

m: Witheringly scornful; severely critical.
t: A scathing review leaves scars: « cinglant ».

m: So delicate as to be difficult to analyze; clever and indirect.
t: Same as « subtil »: finely woven.

m: Existing only on the surface; lacking depth.
t: Same as « superficiel ».

m: To accept something reluctantly but without protest.
t: Same as « acquiescer »: you rest your objections.

m: Clever or skilful, especially in handling difficult situations.
t: Same as « adroit » — even the opposite is French: « maladroit » = inept.

m: To make minor changes to improve; to correct.
t: Same as « amender »: un amendement to a law. Not « emend » (to correct a text).
